title: HAVING Clause
description: Learn how to use the SQL Server HAVING clause to filter grouped results based on specified conditions.

data.text: The HAVING clause filters groups created by the GROUP BY clause based on specified conditions. While WHERE filters individual rows before grouping, HAVING filters groups after aggregation.

data.title: HAVING Clause Syntax
data.content: Filters groups based on conditions applied after aggregation.
data.code:
SELECT
    select_list
FROM
    table_name
GROUP BY
    group_list
HAVING
    conditions;

data.text: The GROUP BY clause summarizes rows into groups, and the HAVING clause applies one or more conditions to these groups. Only groups where the condition evaluates to TRUE are included in the result. Groups that evaluate to FALSE or UNKNOWN are filtered out.

Because SQL Server processes the HAVING clause after the GROUP BY clause, you cannot refer to a column alias defined in the SELECT list within the HAVING clause. Instead, you must use the full aggregate function expression.

data.title: Incorrect: Using Column Alias in HAVING
data.content: This query will fail because the HAVING clause cannot reference the column alias.
data.code:
SELECT
    column_name1,
    column_name2,
    aggregate_function(column_name3) AS column_alias
FROM
    table_name
GROUP BY
    column_name1,
    column_name2
HAVING
    column_alias > value;

data.title: Correct: Using Aggregate Expression in HAVING
data.content: Use the full aggregate function expression instead of the alias.
data.code:
SELECT
    column_name1,
    column_name2,
    aggregate_function(column_name3) AS alias
FROM
    table_name
GROUP BY
    column_name1,
    column_name2
HAVING
    aggregate_function(column_name3) > value;

data.text: The following query finds customers who placed at least two orders per year.

data.title: HAVING with COUNT
data.content: Filters groups to include only customers with two or more orders per year.
data.code:
SELECT
    customer_id,
    YEAR(order_date) AS order_year,
    COUNT(order_id) AS order_count
FROM
    sales.orders
GROUP BY
    customer_id,
    YEAR(order_date)
HAVING
    COUNT(order_id) >= 2
ORDER BY
    customer_id;

data.alt: SQL Server HAVING clause example output

data.text: The following query finds sales orders whose net values exceed 20,000.

data.title: HAVING with SUM
data.content: Filters sales orders to include only those with a net value greater than 20,000.
data.code:
SELECT
    order_id,
    SUM(
        quantity * list_price * (1 - discount)
    ) AS net_value
FROM
    sales.order_items
GROUP BY
    order_id
HAVING
    SUM(
        quantity * list_price * (1 - discount)
    ) > 20000
ORDER BY
    net_value;

data.alt: SQL Server HAVING with SUM example output

data.text: HAVING with MIN, MAX, and AVG
The following query finds product categories where the maximum list price exceeds 4,000 or the minimum list price is below 500.

data.title: HAVING with MIN and MAX
data.content: Filters product categories by their price range.
data.code:
SELECT
    category_id,
    MAX(list_price) AS max_list_price,
    MIN(list_price) AS min_list_price
FROM
    production.products
GROUP BY
    category_id
HAVING
    MAX(list_price) > 4000 OR MIN(list_price) < 500;

data.alt: SQL Server HAVING with MIN and MAX example output

data.text: You can also use HAVING with AVG to find categories whose average prices fall within a specific range.

data.title: HAVING with AVG
data.content: Finds categories with average list prices between 500 and 1,000.
data.code:
SELECT
    category_id,
    AVG(list_price) AS avg_list_price
FROM
    production.products
GROUP BY
    category_id
HAVING
    AVG(list_price) BETWEEN 500 AND 1000;

data.alt: SQL Server HAVING with AVG example output

data.title: HAVING Clause Key Points
points: Use HAVING to filter groups based on aggregate conditions.
HAVING is processed after GROUP BY, while WHERE is processed before.
Do not use column aliases in the HAVING clause; repeat the aggregate expression instead.
HAVING can be used alone (without GROUP BY) to filter based on aggregate conditions over the entire result set.
